claim: Turnip crinkle virus contains a T-shaped, ribosome-binding, translation enhancer (TSS) in its 3'UTR that serves as a hub for interactions throughout the region.
source: Turnip crinkle virus contains a T-shaped, ribosome-binding, translation enhancer (TSS) in its 3'UTR that serves as a hub for interactions throughout the region.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by references to previous work throughout the manuscript.

claim: The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) causes the TSS/surrounding region to undergo a conformational shift postulated to inhibit translation.
source: The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) causes the TSS/surrounding region to undergo a conformational shift postulated to inhibit translation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RdRp binding studies and previous work cited in the manuscript.

claim: The unusual stability of pseudoknotted element H4a/Ψ3 required five upstream adenylates.
source: Using optical tweezers (OT) and steered molecular dynamic simulations (SMD), we found that the unusual stability of pseudoknotted element H4a/Ψ3 required five upstream adenylates
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments showing that replacing 5A with 5U eliminated the H4a/Ψ3 rip.

claim: H4a/Ψ3 was necessary for cooperative association of two other hairpins (H5/H4b) in Mg2+.
source: H4a/Ψ3 was necessary for cooperative association of two other hairpins (H5/H4b) in Mg2+
evidence: This is supported by OT data showing that disruption of H4a/Ψ3 eliminated cooperative unfolding of H4b and H5.

claim: SMD recapitulated the TSS unfolding order in the absence of Mg2+.
source: SMD recapitulated the TSS unfolding order in the absence of Mg2+
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational simulations that matched experimental OT results.

claim: Adenylate mutations eliminated one-site RdRp binding to the 3'UTR.
source: Adenylate mutations eliminated one-site RdRp binding to the 3'UTR, suggesting that RdRp binding to the adenylates disrupts H4a/Ψ3
evidence: This is supported by filter binding assays showing loss of specific RdRp binding when 5A is mutated.

claim: RdRp binding to the adenylates disrupts H4a/Ψ3, leading to loss of H5/H4b interaction and promoting a conformational switch interrupting translation and promoting replication.
source: suggesting that RdRp binding to the adenylates disrupts H4a/Ψ3, leading to loss of H5/H4b interaction and promoting a conformational switch interrupting translation and promoting replication.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the integration of multiple experimental findings.

claim: TCV is a positive-strand RNA virus (genus Carmovirus, family Tombusviridae) with a single uncapped, non-poly(A) genome of 4053 nt encoding five proteins.
source: TCV is a positive-strand RNA virus (genus Carmovirus, family Tombusviridae) with a single uncapped, non-poly(A) genome of 4053 nt encoding five proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TCV cited from previous literature.

claim: The TCV 3'UTR contains at least five hairpins (H4, H4a, H4b, H5 and Pr) and three critical H-type pseudoknots (Ψ1, Ψ2, Ψ3).
source: The TCV 3'UTR contains at least five hairpins (H4, H4a, H4b, H5 and Pr) and three critical H-type pseudoknots (Ψ1, Ψ2, Ψ3) (McCormack et al., 2008; Simon and Miller, 2013)
evidence: This structural information is cited from previous publications.

claim: The coaxially stacked double pseudoknots H4a/Ψ3 and H4b/Ψ2 in conjunction with hairpin H5 fold into a T-shaped structure known as the TSS.
source: The coaxially stacked double pseudoknots H4a/Ψ3 and H4b/Ψ2 in conjunction with hairpin H5 fold into a T-shaped structure known as the TSS (McCormack et al., 2008).
evidence: This structural description is cited from previous work.

claim: The TSS serves as a 3'CITE by binding to 80S ribosomes at the P-site through an interaction with the 60S ribosomal subunit.
source: The TSS serves as a 3'CITE by binding to 80S ribosomes at the P-site through an interaction with the 60S ribosomal subunit (Stupina et al., 2008).
evidence: This functional information is cited from previous work.

claim: Alterations of individual adenylates in the 5A region reduced gRNA levels to between 23% and 55% of wt.
source: Alterations of individual adenylates reduced gRNA levels to between 23% and 55% of wt (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through protoplast transfection experiments.

claim: Dinucleotide alterations made step-wise throughout 5A were previously shown to be equally detrimental to TCV fitness, with each mutant gRNA accumulating to less than 5% of wt levels in Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts.
source: Dinucleotide alterations made step-wise throughout 5A were previously shown to be equally detrimental to TCV fitness, with each mutant gRNA accumulating to less than 5% of wt levels in Arabidopsis thaliana protoplasts (Yuan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Converting all five adenylates in TSS118 to uridylates (construct 5AtoU) caused selected residues in the 5A region and surrounding sequences to display flexibility differences of >25% compared with wt.
source: As shown in Figures 1C and D, and quantified in Figure 1F, selected residues in the 5A region and surrounding sequences of 5AtoU, as well as residues within the H4a loop, displayed flexibility differences of >25% compared with wt.
evidence: This is demonstrated through in-line probing experiments.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, the TSS unfolded with three transitions corresponding to hairpins H4a, H4b, and H5.
source: In the absence of Mg2+, the TSS was expected to unfold with three transitions, corresponding to hairpins H4a, H4b, and H5.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers force-extension curves.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, H4b unfolded first, followed by H5 and then H4a/Ψ3.
source: In the absence of Mg2+, H4b unfolded first, followed by H5 and then H4a/Ψ3, which had been predicted to be the least stable element.
evidence: This unfolding order was determined through optical tweezers experiments using complementary oligonucleotides.

claim: In the presence of Mg2+, H4b unfolded cooperatively with H5, followed by H4a/Ψ3.
source: In the presence of Mg2+, H4b unfolded cooperatively with H5, followed by H4a/Ψ3.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments showing a large cooperative rip (1*).

claim: Mg2+ was not required to form H4a/Ψ3 but enhanced the stability of H4a/Ψ3 and all other elements tested.
source: Mg2+ was not required to form H4a/Ψ3 but enhanced the stability of H4a/Ψ3 and all other elements tested.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments showing H4a/Ψ3 forms in the absence of Mg2+ but requires higher force to unfold in its presence.

claim: Disrupting H4a/Ψ3 eliminated the cooperative unfolding of H4b and H5.
source: Disrupting H4a/Ψ3 eliminated the cooperative unfolding of H4b and H5
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments with the mH4a mutant.

claim: H4a/Ψ3 was unstable in the absence of the upstream stretch of five adenylates.
source: H4a/Ψ3 was unstable in the absence of the upstream stretch of five adenylates.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments showing no H4a/Ψ3 rip when 5A is replaced with 5U.

claim: Mutating two of the five adenylates or adjacent downstream residues eliminated specific binding of RdRp to a 3'UTR fragment.
source: Mutating two of these adenylates or adjacent downstream residues eliminated specific binding of RdRp to a 3'UTR fragment
evidence: This is demonstrated through filter binding assays.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, H4b unfolded at 10 to 13.5 pN.
source: In the absence of Mg2+, H4b unfolded at 10 to 13.5 pN
evidence: This is determined through force clamping experiments.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, H5 unfolded at 13 to 15.5 pN.
source: H5 at 13 to 15.5 pN
evidence: This is determined through force clamping experiments.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, H4a/Ψ3 unfolded at 14.5 to 18.5 pN.
source: H4a/Ψ3 at 14.5 to 18.5 pN (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is determined through force clamping experiments.

claim: Mg2+ increased the mechanical stability of all TSS elements.
source: Mg2+ increased the mechanical stability of all TSS elements
evidence: This is demonstrated through force clamping experiments showing higher unfolding forces in the presence of Mg2+.

claim: In Mg2+, H4b unfolded between 13 and 16.5 pN.
source: with H4b now unfolding between 13 and 16.5 pN
evidence: This is determined through force clamping experiments in the presence of Mg2+.

claim: In Mg2+, H5 unfolded from 14.5 to 17.5 pN.
source: H5 from 14.5 to 17.5 pN
evidence: This is determined through force clamping experiments in the presence of Mg2+.

claim: In Mg2+, H4a/Ψ3 unfolded from 16.5 to 18 pN.
source: H4a/Ψ3 from 16.5 to 18 pN (Figure 4B
evidence: This is determined through force clamping experiments in the presence of Mg2+.

claim: The experimental contour length of H4b in the absence of Mg2+ was 15.3 ± 1.5 nm.
source: In the absence of Mg2+, the contour length of H4b was estimated to be 16.0 nm and the experimental length was 15.3 ± 1.5 nm.
evidence: This is measured through force clamping experiments.

claim: The experimental contour length of H5 in the absence of Mg2+ was 17.0 ± 1.8 nm.
source: The estimated length of H5 was 24.8 nm and the experimental length was 17.0 ± 1.8 nm
evidence: This is measured through force clamping experiments.

claim: The experimental contour length of H4a/Ψ3 in the absence of Mg2+ was 9.1 ± 1.5 nm.
source: For H4a/Ψ3, the estimated length was 13.6 nm and the experimental length in the absence of Mg2+ was 9.1 ± 1.5 nm.
evidence: This is measured through force clamping experiments.

claim: The difference between the estimated and observed lengths of H5 may reflect instability of the H5 lower stem.
source: The difference between the estimated and observed lengths of H5 may reflect instability of the H5 lower stem (~5.9 nm) (McCormack et al., 2008), which might unfold at a lower force as suggested by the SMD simulations
evidence: This is inferred from the discrepancy between predicted and measured contour lengths and supported by SMD simulations.

claim: A single H4a/Ψ3 transition was observed in 10 mM Mg2+ near the position of rip 3 for a truncated fragment containing only H4a/Ψ3, 5A, and flanking residues.
source: A single H4a/Ψ3 transition was observed in 10 mM Mg2+ near the position of rip 3 (Figure 3B, left), suggesting that H4a/Ψ3 can form in the absence of H4b and H5.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments on a truncated fragment.

claim: The critical force required to unfold H4a/Ψ3 was 19.95 ± 0.06 pN in 10 mM Mg2+.
source: The critical force required to unfold H4a/Ψ3 was 19.95 ± 0.06 pN (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is measured through force ramping experiments.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+ and presence of 10 mM or 250 mM NaCl, the H4a/Ψ3 rip was present at forces that were 4 to 5 pN lower than in Mg2+.
source: In the absence of Mg2+ and presence of 10 mM or 250 mM NaCl, the single rip was present at forces that were 4 to 5 pN lower (Figure 3A, right; Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments under different ionic conditions.

claim: Mg2+ enhances the stability of the folded H4a/Ψ3 structure, similar to what was found for the BWYV pseudoknot.
source: suggesting that Mg2+ enhances the stability of the folded structure, similar to what was found for the BWYV pseudoknot (Grilley et al., 2006).
evidence: This is inferred from the force measurements and compared to cited literature.

claim: Replacing 5A with 5U in the truncated fragment eliminated the H4a/Ψ3 rip in the presence and absence of Mg2+.
source: Replacing 5A with 5U in the truncated fragment (fragment 5A5U) eliminated the H4a/Ψ3 rip in the presence (Figure 3C) and absence (data not shown) of Mg2+.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments.

claim: 5A is required to both form and stabilize H4a/Ψ3.
source: Since no other transitions were observed, this result suggests that 5A is required to both form and stabilize H4a/Ψ3.
evidence: This is inferred from the elimination of the H4a/Ψ3 rip when 5A is replaced with 5U.

claim: Recombinant TCV RdRp bound to the wt 3' fragment with a Kd = 2.6 μM.
source: Recombinant TCV RdRp bound to the wt fragment with a Kd = 2.6 μM (Figure 7).
evidence: This is measured through filter binding assays.

claim: RdRp did not exhibit specific one-site binding to MDV (midivariant RNA, 221 nt), which is a non-template satellite RNA associated with Qβ bacteriophage.
source: In contrast, RdRp did not exhibit specific one-site binding to MDV (midivariant RNA, 221 nt), which is a non-template satellite RNA associated with Qβ bacteriophage.
evidence: This is demonstrated through filter binding assays showing non-specific binding.

claim: A two nucleotide mutation in 5A at positions 8 and 9 (A to U; m74) prevented specific binding of RdRp to the 3' fragment.
source: A two nucleotide mutation in 5A at positions 8 and 9 (A to U; m74) prevented specific binding of RdRp to the fragment.
evidence: This is demonstrated through filter binding assays.

claim: Two individual alterations in the loop of H4a (m27, m41) improved binding of the RdRp to the template by 2.5-fold.
source: Two individual alterations in the loop of H4a (m27, m41) improved binding of the RdRp to the template by 2.5-fold.
evidence: This is demonstrated through filter binding assays.

claim: Mutations in the two partner residues of m27 and m41 located just downstream of 5A (m26, m40) eliminated one-site binding to the template.
source: In contrast, mutations in the two partner residues of m27 and m41 located just downstream of 5A (m26, m40) eliminated one-site binding to the template (Figure 7).
evidence: This is demonstrated through filter binding assays.

claim: Deletion of H4 (ΔH4) had no significant effect on RdRp binding.
source: Deletion of H4 (ΔH4) had no significant effect on RdRp binding, suggesting that the binding region may be confined to the sequence between H4 and H4a.
evidence: This is demonstrated through filter binding assays and leads to an inference about the binding region.

claim: The RdRp may be specifically interacting with 5A and adjacent downstream sequences.
source: These results suggest that disruption of H4a/Ψ3 (which occurs when the adenylates are altered in m74) is not the proximal cause of the loss of specific RdRp binding, but rather the RdRp may be specifically interacting with 5A and adjacent downstream sequences
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of mutations that affect RdRp binding.

claim: RdRp interaction with 5A may be facilitated by the absence of Ψ3.
source: this interaction may be facilitated by the absence of Ψ3.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutations disrupting Ψ3 improve RdRp binding.

claim: In 70% to 100% of the SMD simulations with a constant pulling speed of 0.01 Å/ps, H4a/Ψ3 opened last.
source: In 70% to 100% of the SMD simulations (depending on the parameters used) with a constant pulling speed of 0.01 Å/ps, H4a/Ψ3 opened last
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational simulations.

claim: In 40% to 50% of all the SMD simulations, the full sequence of events was in agreement with the experimental OT results (H4b opening first, H5 second, and H4a/Ψ3 last).
source: in 40% to 50% of all the simulations, the full sequence of events was in agreement with the experimental OT results (H4b opening first, H5 second, and H4a/Ψ3 last).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational simulations.

claim: The structural resistance to pulling is increased for the TSS pseudoknotted motifs beyond their free energy predictions by their orientation parallel to the direction of pulling.
source: Computer simulations of the unfolding pathway support this hypothesis by indicating that the structural resistance to pulling is increased for the TSS pseudoknotted motifs beyond their free energy predictions by their orientation parallel (and nearly co-axial) to the direction of pulling
evidence: This is inferred from SMD simulations.

claim: The basal TSS conformation did not change substantially when bound to ribosomes.
source: The basal TSS conformation did not change substantially when bound to ribosomes (Stupina et al., 2011)
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: The TSS was significantly altered when a 3'UTR fragment or a 320 nt 3' terminal fragment was bound by the RdRp.
source: but was significantly altered when a 3'UTR fragment (252 nt) or a 320 nt 3' terminal fragment was bound by the RdRp (Yuan et al., 2009, 2012).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Prominent changes upon RdRp binding included enhanced flexibility of hairpin H3 in the coat protein ORF and adjacent upstream sequences.
source: Prominent changes included enhanced flexibility of: (1) hairpin H3 in the coat protein ORF and adjacent upstream sequences
evidence: This is cited from previous work on RdRp binding effects.

claim: Prominent changes upon RdRp binding included enhanced flexibility of the terminal loop of hairpin H4 located just upstream of the TSS.
source: (2) the terminal loop of hairpin H4 located just upstream of the TSS
evidence: This is cited from previous work on RdRp binding effects.

claim: Prominent changes upon RdRp binding included enhanced flexibility of H4a/Ψ3 in the TSS.
source: (3) H4a/Ψ3 in the TSS.
evidence: This is cited from previous work on RdRp binding effects.

claim: Sequences with reduced flexibility upon RdRp binding included the 5' side of the basal stem of H5.
source: Sequences with reduced flexibility included: (1) the 5' side of the basal stem of H5
evidence: This is cited from previous work on RdRp binding effects.

claim: Sequences with reduced flexibility upon RdRp binding included the sequence between H4b and H5.
source: (2) the sequence between H4b and H5
evidence: This is cited from previous work on RdRp binding effects.

claim: Sequences with reduced flexibility upon RdRp binding included the A-rich sequence upstream of H4a.
source: (3) the A-rich sequence upstream of H4a.
evidence: This is cited from previous work on RdRp binding effects.

claim: A mechanism exists for the TSS to transition between conformations required for translation and replication after a threshold level of RdRp was available.
source: These findings suggested that a mechanism exists for the TSS to transition between conformations required for translation and replication after a threshold level of RdRp was available.
evidence: This is inferred from previous findings on RdRp-induced conformational changes.

claim: H4a alone is not stable in the absence of Ψ3 and/or other surrounding sequences.
source: When a fragment containing only H4a (positions 13 to 37) was subjected to OT, no rips were observed, suggesting that H4a is not stable in the absence of Ψ3 and/or other surrounding sequences (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments on an H4a-only fragment.

claim: H4a/Ψ3 can form in the absence of H4b and H5.
source: A single H4a/Ψ3 transition was observed in 10 mM Mg2+ near the position of rip 3 (Figure 3B, left), suggesting that H4a/Ψ3 can form in the absence of H4b and H5.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments on a truncated fragment.

claim: In the presence of Mg2+, H4b and H5 exhibited cooperative unfolding in FECs.
source: In Mg2+, H4b and H5 exhibited cooperative unfolding in FECs (rip 1*; Figure 2B)
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers force-extension curves.

claim: In Mg2+, H4b and H5 had overlapping unfolding forces in force clamping.
source: and had overlapping unfolding forces in force clamping (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through force clamping experiments.

claim: When H4a/Ψ3 was eliminated (fragment mH4a), rip 1* was replaced with individual H4b and H5 rips.
source: In addition, when H4a/Ψ3 was eliminated (fragment mH4a), rip 1* was replaced with individual H4b and H5 rips, suggesting that H4b and H5 were no longer cooperatively unfolding in the absence of H4a/Ψ3 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments with the mH4a mutant.

claim: In the absence of H4a/Ψ3, H4b and H5 transitions were less cooperative and similar to those found in the absence of Mg2+.
source: In the absence of H4a/Ψ3, H4b and H5 transitions were less cooperative and now similar to those found in the absence of Mg2+.
evidence: This is demonstrated through force clamping experiments with the mH4a mutant.

claim: In the absence of H4a/Ψ3, H4b unfolded at a lower force range (with multiple hops observed at 13.5 pN compared with 15 pN).
source: H4b also unfolded at a lower force range (with multiple hops observed at 13.5 pN compared with 15 pN)
evidence: This is demonstrated through force clamping experiments with the mH4a mutant.

claim: In the absence of H4a/Ψ3, H4b contained a shorter contour length (11.3 ± 1.1 nm compared with 15.8 nm).
source: and contained a shorter contour length (11.3 ± 1.1 nm compared with 15.8 nm).
evidence: This is measured through force clamping experiments with the mH4a mutant.

claim: A new 7.38 ± 0.98 nm transition ('Ψ2') was observed between 10 and 13.5 pN in the mH4a mutant, which could represent unfolding of Ψ2 and the first few bases of the H4b stem.
source: A new 7.38 ± 0.98 nm transition ('Ψ2') was also observed between 10 and 13.5 pN (Figure 6A), which could represent unfolding of Ψ2 and the first few bases of the H4b stem.
evidence: This is observed through force clamping experiments and interpreted based on the measured contour length.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, H4a/Ψ3 hopping was no longer observed when H5 was eliminated.
source: In the absence of Mg2+, H4a/Ψ3 hopping was no longer observed (Figure 6B)
evidence: This is demonstrated through force clamping experiments with H5 disrupted.

claim: In the absence of Mg2+, H5 is needed to stabilize H4a/Ψ3 under force clamping conditions.
source: suggesting that, in the absence of Mg2+, H5 is needed to stabilize H4a/Ψ3 under force clamping conditions (but not force ramping since rip 3 is still present in H5-disrupted FECs [Figure 2B] and when using a fragment containing only 5A/H4a/Ψ3 [Figure 3B]).
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of H4a/Ψ3 hopping when H5 is disrupted, with the caveat noted about force ramping.

claim: Disrupting H5 caused H4b to start unfolding at a lower force (11.5 pN) in the presence and absence of Mg2+.
source: In addition, disrupting H5 caused H4b to start unfolding at a lower force (11.5 pN) in the presence and absence of Mg2+ (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through force clamping experiments with H5 disrupted.

claim: Mg2+ stabilizes interactions between H4a/Ψ3 and H4b/H5, and between H4b and H5.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that Mg2+ stabilizes interactions between H4a/Ψ3 and H4b/H5, and between H4b and H5.
evidence: This is inferred from the collective results of force clamping experiments under different conditions.

claim: The 3' region of the TCV gRNA adopts an alternative conformation upon binding to the RdRp, which significantly affects the structure of the TSS and other nearby elements.
source: As described above, the 3' region of the TCV gRNA adopts an alternative conformation upon binding to the RdRp, which significantly affects the structure of the TSS and other nearby elements (Yuan et al., 2010, 2009).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: One consequence of RdRp binding to fragments containing the TSS was reduced flexibility of 5A residues.
source: One consequence of RdRp binding to fragments containing the TSS was reduced flexibility of 5A residues, suggesting that this motif might be a target site for the RdRp (Yuan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from previous work and used to support a hypothesis.

claim: The ability of the RdRp to continue transcribing low levels of complementary strands in the absence of 5A binding is likely due to the presence of the 3' terminal Pr hairpin, which in combination with upstream hairpin H4 can promote a low level of transcription.
source: The ability of the RdRp to continue transcribing low levels of complementary strands in the absence of 5A binding is likely due to the presence of the 3' terminal Pr hairpin, which in combination with upstream hairpin H4 can promote a low level of transcription (Sun and Simon, 2006).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of residual transcription and cited previous work.

claim: Explicit solvent MD simulations of nucleic acids are considered to be more accurate as all water/salt atoms around the solute are accounted for in the simulation.
source: Explicit solvent MD simulations of nucleic acids are considered to be more accurate as all water/salt atoms around the solute are accounted for in the simulation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about computational methods.

claim: Pulling speed affected the orientation of helices relative to the direction of pulling.
source: The key observation based on these simulations was that pulling speed affected the orientation of helices relative to the direction of pulling (refer to Appendix 1 for more details).
evidence: This is observed through SMD simulations at different pulling speeds.

claim: Formation of new, transient tertiary interactions by H4b after all hydrogen bonds between H4b and Ψ2 opened increased the resistance to pulling and impacted the order of TSS unfolding.
source: This led to formation of new, transient tertiary interactions by H4b after all hydrogen bonds between H4b and Ψ2 opened, increasing the resistance to pulling and impacting the order of TSS unfolding.
evidence: This is observed through SMD simulations.

claim: Introducing a pause in the pulling simulation immediately after Ψ2 opening to re-equilibrate the system and avoid transient H4b interactions changed the order of TSS opening events to H4b opening first, followed by H5 and then H4a.
source: Introducing a pause in the pulling simulation immediately after Ψ2 opening to re-equilibrate the system and avoid transient H4b interactions changed the order of TSS opening events to H4b opening first, followed by H5 and then H4a.
evidence: This is demonstrated through modified SMD simulations.

claim: The demonstrated applicability of the implicit solvent MD to optical tweezers pulling simulations of highly structured nucleic acids is novel.
source: The demonstrated applicability of the implicit solvent MD to optical tweezers pulling simulations of highly structureed nucleic acids is novel in its own right, and worth noting as such.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the methodological approach.

claim: In the new TSS model, A7 through A10 help to support Ψ3, which is extended to include the A11–U26 base pair.
source: In the new TSS model (Figure 1E), A7 through A10 help to support Ψ3, which is extended to include the A11–U26 base pair
evidence: This is based on the structural model derived from MD simulations.

claim: The triple interactions formed by A7 through A10 did not offer much resistance to pulling.
source: but the triple interactions that they form did not offer much resistance to pulling.
evidence: This is observed through SMD simulations.

claim: H4a/Ψ3 may be highly stable due to its coaxially stacked stems, creating base-pair planes perpendicular to the direction of the unfolding force requiring high force to overcome resistance of multiple base pairs at the same time.
source: H4a/Ψ3 may also be highly stable due to its coaxially stacked stems, creating base-pair planes perpendicular to the direction of the unfolding force requiring high force to overcome resistance of multiple base pairs at the same time.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement and supported by SMD simulations.

claim: Ψ3 opens gradually and, as the entire Ψ3 motif opens, transient tertiary interactions outside of the original Ψ3 base pairs maintain the pseudoknot topology, thus increasing the resistance to pulling and delaying the opening of H4a/Ψ3.
source: For example, Ψ3 opens gradually and, as the entire Ψ3 motif opens, transient tertiary interactions outside of the original Ψ3 base pairs maintain the pseudoknot topology, thus increasing the resistance to pulling and delaying the opening of H4a/Ψ3.
evidence: This is observed through SMD simulations.

claim: Mg2+ is important for stabilizing RNA tertiary structures.
source: Mg2+ is important for stabilizing RNA tertiary structures (Draper, 2004; Pyle, 2002; Tan and Chen, 2011; Woodson, 2005)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from the literature.

claim: Mg2+ has been shown to be a key factor in controlling conformational switches in a number of RNAs.
source: and has been shown to be a key factor in controlling conformational switches in a number of RNAs (Choudhary and Sigel, 2014; Reining et al., 2013; Suddala et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from the literature.

claim: Stability of all three TSS transitions increased by 2 to 3 pN over the force required in the absence of Mg2+.
source: In addition, stability of all three TSS transitions increased by 2 to 3 pN over the force required in the absence of Mg2+ (Figures 4 and 6)
evidence: This is measured through force clamping experiments.

claim: Fully stretched H4a/Ψ3 (13 nm) was only obtained in Mg2+ at high force (≥18 pN).
source: and fully stretched H4a/Ψ3 (13 nm) was only obtained in Mg2+ at high force (≥18 pN) (Figure 5).
evidence: This is measured through force clamping experiments.

claim: Mg2+ increases the kinetic barriers to the mechanical unfolding of the TSS elements.
source: These results imply that Mg2+ increases the kinetic barriers to the mechanical unfolding of the TSS elements.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased forces required for unfolding in the presence of Mg2+.

claim: The presence of Mg2+ increased the stability of H4b and H4a/Ψ3 and suppressed their unfolding.
source: indicating that the presence of Mg2+ increased the stability of these elements and suppressed their unfolding.
evidence: This is inferred from the abrupt changes in hopping behavior observed in force clamping experiments.

claim: The TSS experimentally assumes a conformation compatible with ribosome binding in the absence of the RdRp.
source: This could explain the refolding dynamics of the TSS, which experimentally assumes a conformation compatible with ribosome binding in the absence of the RdRp (Yuan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from previous work and used to interpret the current findings.

claim: Disruption of either H4b or H5 led to the disappearance of rip 1*.
source: For example, disruption of either H4b or H5 led to the disappearance of rip 1* (Figures 2C and D), indicating cooperative unfolding of the two hairpins.
evidence: This is demonstrated through optical tweezers experiments.

claim: A connection between H5 and H4b was previously suggested by finding second-site mutations in H4b when the lower bulge loop of H5 was mutated.
